title: CHRONOBERG: CAPTURING LANGUAGE EVOLUTION AND TEMPORAL AWARENESS IN FOUNDATION MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating large language models and hate speech classifiers across 50-year historical intervals (1750-2000) by comparing their predictions against historically calibrated Valence-Arousal-Dominance (VAD) lexicons, and measuring LLM perplexity on valence-shifting vs. valence-stable words.

Analyzing discrepancies between modern hate speech detection tools (e.g., RoBERTa, Perspective API, OpenAI) and historically calibrated sentiment scores on historical sentences containing racial and ethnic group mentions.
Evaluating modern hate speech classifiers' contextual interpretation of historical texts involving women and gender-specific terminology (e.g., 'hussy') across different time periods.
Assessing how modern hate-check tools classify historically context-dependent words (e.g., 'gay', 'faggot') that have undergone significant diachronic semantic shifts over the past 250 years.
